summary.headline: Marathon Nextgen Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue INR145 crore and PAT INR45 crore; Monte South stake to rise from 40% to 100% for INR335 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated total revenue of INR145 crore, EBITDA of INR61 crore and PAT of INR45 crore, with H1 revenue of INR362 crore and PAT of INR98 crore. Pre-sales on the existing portfolio rose to INR154 crore in Q2 from INR86 crore in Q1, with collections of INR127 crore. The Board approved buying Adani Group's 60% stake in Monte South for INR335 crore (INR200 crore already paid), taking Marathon's ownership from 40% to 100%, with completion expected this quarter. The company said it ended September with a net debt-free balance sheet and a positive net cash position.

segments.name: Residential - affordable and mid-income
segments.commentary: Bookings of INR80 crore vs INR31 crore in Q1; about 51,800 sq ft sold vs 22,100 sq ft in Q1.

segments.name: Monte South (Byculla, 40% share)
segments.commentary: Company's 40% share of sales about 15,800 sq ft with booking value INR58 crore (up from INR50 crore in Q1) and collections of INR57 crore. Tower A has full OC; Tower B OC up to 45th floor.

segments.name: Marathon Nexzone, Panvel
segments.commentary: Area sold about 28,200 sq ft (doubled), booking value INR39 crore vs INR17 crore in Q1; Phase 3 contributed over 10,000 sq ft.

segments.name: Bhandup (NeoValley, NeoPark, NeoSquare)
segments.commentary: Area sold about 23,600 sq ft vs 8,300 sq ft in Q1; booking value nearly tripled to INR41 crore from INR15 crore; collections INR30 crore vs INR18 crore.

segments.name: Commercial (Marathon Futurex, combined with merged portfolio)
segments.commentary: About 21,700 sq ft sold vs 4,000 sq ft in Q1; booking value INR107 crore vs INR19 crore; collections INR91 crore. A financial services occupier expanded by about 45,000 sq ft.

guidance_outlook: Monte South acquisition (INR335 crore, Adani's 60% stake) expected to complete in Q3 FY27; full 100% revenue to be consolidated from the next quarter.
Management said Monte South sales were about INR300 crore so far and could reach about INR600 crore in the year on current run rate; it declined to give a forward annual presales run-rate target.
Monte South remaining bookings of about INR7,000 crore to be recognised over roughly a 4-year period after each launch; surplus of about INR2,100 crore cited at 30%+ EBITDA margin.
Launch pipeline: Monte South commercial (GDV about INR3,400 crore) in FY28; Tower D (GDV about INR1,800 crore) in FY29; Bhandup projects (GDV INR1,000 crore or more) over FY28-29.
Three new projects (Versova, Sewri, Kanjur) add combined GDV of about INR1,740 crore; management said Versova and Sewri together about INR900 crore and both to launch within two financial years.
Proposed amalgamation: NSE/BSE no-adverse-observation letter filed with NCLT; creditor/shareholder meetings reported positive; NCLT hearing scheduled in November 2026.
capex_capacity: Monte South: Tower A fully occupied; Tower B OC up to 45th floor with RCC completed up to terrace; Tower C complete up to 35th floor; Tower B balance construction cost about INR200 crore.
Panvel: Cedar and Daffodil towers have full OC; Phase 3 excavation and footing nearly complete, plinth slab for 2 towers nearing completion.

Bhandup: NeoValley Kaveri 100% RCC complete, internal walls and clustering 95%; NeoValley Wing A 95% RCC; NeoValley Narmada A wing (rehab) RCC done, finishing 60%; Narmada B at 4th slab; Narmada C at plinth; NeoPark Ashoka A and B ready up to 22 floors, 30% complete; Ashoka C at 21st slab.
Management said project launches depend on approvals, land acquisition and conversion; a 'bigger bang' of launches is being prepared over the next few quarters.
Redevelopment approvals (environmental clearance and government approval) typically take 8-12 months, per management.
demand_pricing: Monte South sales growing quarter-on-quarter; management cited about 800 of roughly 1,800 apartments sold and said redevelopment inventory is not competing with the product.
Management said prices at Monte South rose about 10% over the last year across towers; Tower A (ready) commands a higher price than Tower B and Tower C.
Panvel demand driven by conversions from eastern Mumbai micro markets (Sewri, Mazgaon), with management saying those locations realise more than 2x Panvel prices.
Sales recorded only on registration; management said cheques collected in Bhandup will reflect in the coming quarters.
Commercial demand at Futurex supported by HNI clients from residential projects; Monte South commercial tower to be brought forward.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors view remaining development potential and opportunity from moving to 100% ownership of Monte South?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the project is about 25 lakh sq ft, of which about 10 lakh sq ft is sold and about 15 lakh sq ft remains; GDV about INR10,000 crore, with about INR3,000 crore sold and about INR7,000 crore to be recognised, implying about INR2,100 crore surplus at 30%+ EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is Monte South facing demand slowdown or supply pressure from redevelopment projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Kaivalya Shah said sales were strong even in the rainy season, with about INR146 crore in Q2 at Monte South, and that the redevelopment inventory is not competing with this luxury product; he cited about 800 of 1,800 units sold.

qa_highlights.question: What are the launch plans for H2 FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management listed Monte South commercial (GDV about INR3,400 crore) for FY28, Tower D (about INR1,800 crore) for FY29, Bhandup projects (about INR1,000 crore or more) and Panvel Phase 3 (about INR600 crore, already launched); no Q2 launches, as approvals and land work are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Why were there no launches in Q2 and what holds back the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said launches depend on approvals, land acquisition and conversion; several files are in approval and a larger set of launches is being prepared for the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for monetising Tower D and the commercial component of Monte South?
qa_highlights.answer: The commercial tower is to launch next financial year and take about 4 to 5 years to complete; after launch, one tower takes about 4 years and the second is deferred by 1 to 1.5 years, depending on absorption.

qa_highlights.question: Will residential presales momentum in affordable and mid-income continue in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Panvel is expected to add meaningful affordable sales in coming quarters, with Bhandup bookings reflecting as registrations complete.

qa_highlights.question: How are approvals and execution risk handled for Versova, Sewri and Kanjurmarg redevelopment projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said society awards take time after multi-round bidding; environmental and government approvals take about 8 to 12 months; Kanjurmarg is already under construction and contributed profit in Q1 and Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Can Monte South realisations improve given Mumbai premium demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Chetan Shah said prices have firmed, with about 10% increase over the last 12 months in each tower segment; Tower A (ready) fetches the highest price.

risks_watch: Completion timing of the INR335 crore Monte South acquisition (INR200 crore already paid) and the consolidation step-up from 40% to 100% from next quarter.
Pending NCLT hearing on the proposed amalgamation, which is subject to regulatory approval.
Launch timing depends on approvals (8-12 months for redevelopment), land acquisition and conversion; no launches recorded in Q2.
Management declined to give forward annual presales guidance; the INR600 crore Monte South full-year estimate is an extrapolation of current run rate.
Pre-sales are recognised on registration, so cheque-based bookings in Bhandup may lag in reported numbers.
Cost to complete Tower B cited at about INR200 crore; project EBITDA margin cited at 30-35%.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Monte South sales momentum and the 100% ownership step-up, with specific figures given freely. Cautious on forward guidance: declined to give a future annual presales run-rate and framed launch timing as dependent on approvals.
key_quotes: The quarter-on-quarter performance is encouraging because it shows improved demand across different price segments within our portfolio, supported by our presence in established Mumbai micro markets.
We ended September with a net debt-free balance sheet and a positive net cash position.
So now from the next quarter onwards, when the acquisition gets completed, the full revenue of 100% gets consolidated in our books.
